all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The Enterprise Development Programme provides innovation assistance in the form of grants up to one-half of product development costs for small firms, while also offering loan guarantees to help vulnerable industries meet increased import competition.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Providing grants and loan guarantees supports small firms in innovation, enhancing their competitiveness.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The programme is stated to be providing assistance.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The programme offers significant support to small firms, indicating a notable but not transformative impact.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The Enterprise Development Programme...provides innovation assistance in the form of grants up to one-half (or three-quarters for small firms) of product development costs.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The reform is only identified by one model and lacks a clear government adoption signal, making it uncertain.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The Canadian government announced measures in the April 1978 budget and reinforced them in the November 1978 budget to stimulate research and development expenditure, providing increased investment and R&D incentives to support corporate investment in R&D. These measures were introduced in response to recommendations from the First Ministers' Conference task forces.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax incentives and direct investment support increase private sector R&D capacity and productivity, supporting innovation and long-term economic growth.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: Text states measures were 'announced' in April 1978 budget and November 1978 budget; no evidence of implementation provided.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: Significant fiscal measures announced across two budgets in 1978 to stimulate R&D, but not a structural system-wide reform.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The Government agreed in principle with the vast majority of these proposals, and in the November 1978 Budget responded to several of the recommendations, including the provision of increased investment as well as research and development incentives.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: This reform is only identified by one model and while it discusses 'increased investment and R&D incentives', it lacks a clear current context or government adoption signal.
